newsitem.title: USA: U.S. dealers take two cents HRW wheat protection.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dealers take two cents HRW wheat protection.

text.p: U.S. cash grain dealers said they were taking two cents per bushel cash protection on hard red winter wheat in anticipation of a lower KCBT opening.
"Everyone is taking a bit of protection," one Kansas merchandiser said. "We're taking two cents on wheat this morning. Looks like they got some rains in South America."
Grain futures markets were called to open sharply lower after beneficial rains fell in soybean growing regions of Brazil, easing concerns of crop damage, traders said.
Cash dealers said farmer selling remained slow.
"We haven't really bought anything this morning but we're taking two cents (protection) on wheat, four cents on milo, two cents on corn and a nickel on beans," another Kansas merchandiser said.
